title: KV cache quantization and compression experiments (FP8 / INT8 / INT4) — benchmarks and quality trade-offs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Run a controlled set of experiments to evaluate compact KV-cache encodings (FP8, INT8, INT4) for the serving runtime. Goals: quantify GPU memory savings, throughput/latency impact, and end-to-end quality regressions on representative workloads (chat, long-context summarization, retrieval-augmented generation). Produce a recommended hybrid compression strategy and a fallback plan for production rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks for FP8, INT8, INT4 vs baseline FP16 on 7B and 30B model traces with realistic prefix lengths (512, 2048).
Quantified memory savings and per-request latency overhead (p95) for encode/decode on A100 and H100.
Quality deltas: perplexity, generation token-level error rates, and human-annotated failure samples for >1000 seeded prompts.
A proposed rollout plan: config knobs, checks, and canary thresholds + measured thresholds for auto-fallback.
Design doc and PRs merged for safe runtime integration (decompression paths gated behind feature flag).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Kickoff: scoped test matrix and dataset. Using chat-like conversations (1k threads), long-context docs (500 samples), and synthetic stress traces to exercise KV churn. Aisha set up baseline FP16 run and instrumented cache stats.

2026-03-11 - Initial FP8 prototype: per-layer FP8 quantization (dynamic range) implemented in local branch. Memory: ~1.95x reduction vs FP16 for KV storage on 7B; throughput unchanged. Observed ~0.6% perplexity increase on summarization traces.

2026-03-12 - INT8 run: symmetric per-tensor INT8 with per-head scaling. Memory: ~2.0x reduction vs FP16; dequant cost +1.1ms p95 on H100 when dequantizing full KV for each request. Quality: negligible perplexity delta (~0.2%) on chat, but rare token degeneration on long-context tests (0.3% of samples).

2026-03-13 - INT4 compression (aggressive): ~3.9x raw memory reduction vs FP16 (after packing). But quality regressions visible: perplexity +2.8% on average, and 1.7% of threads produced incoherent tokens in rare-token contexts. CPU/GPU overhead increases due to bit-unpacking and per-chunk dequant scaling (~3.8ms p95).

2026-03-13 - Hybrid experiments: storing 'hot' KV (recently used top-k entries) in FP8/INT8 and 'cold' KV in packed INT4 yields 2.7x effective memory reduction with <0.8% average perplexity delta and p95 latency overhead ~1.6ms. This seems promising for Dedicated customers focused on capacity density.

2026-03-14 - Review feedback from Priya (Applied ML): investigate per-head sensitivity — some attention heads are tolerant to INT4 while others amplify noise. Recommendation: head-aware quantization table (hot heads in INT8/FP8, tolerant heads INT4).

2026-03-14 - Security/ops note from Marcus: ensure checksumming and a lightweight integrity marker per compressed blob to detect corruption during transfer between host and GPU memory. Added to next steps.
2026-03-14 - Engineering note: implemented feature flag runtime.kv_quantization.v1 to gate decompression paths. Added basic metrics: kv_bytes_saved, kv_dequant_ms, kv_quality_regressions_count.
results_summary: Baseline: FP16 KV cache on 7B uses ~9.6GB GPU memory for a 2048-token prefix workload.
FP8: ~4.9GB KV (48.9% reduction), p95 latency overhead ~+0.4ms, perplexity delta +0.6% on average.
INT8: ~4.8GB KV (50% reduction), p95 latency overhead ~+1.1ms (dequant), perplexity delta +0.2% but rare long-context token errors (0.3% samples).
INT4 (packed): ~2.5GB KV (~74% reduction), p95 latency overhead ~+3.8ms, perplexity delta +2.8%, 1.7% incoherent samples in stress traces.
Hybrid (FP8/INT8 hot, INT4 cold, per-head tuning): effective ~2.9x reduction (~3.3GB), p95 overhead ~+1.6ms, average perplexity delta <0.8%, failure rate reduced to 0.4% with head-aware mapping.
decisions: Do not enable full-pipeline INT4 compression by default — risk of quality regressions is non-trivial for long-tail queries.
Proceed with a gated hybrid strategy: default FP8 for new Dedicated customers; enable INT4 cold-store as opt-in for customers requiring maximum density after QA and canarying.
Require per-head sensitivity calibration during model onboarding. Store a small head-sensitivity map alongside model metadata to choose per-head quant levels.
Add integrity checks and checksum markers for compressed KV blobs and abort to fallback on any mismatch.
Expose runtime knobs: kv.quant.levels = {hot: FP8, warm: INT8, cold: INT4}, kv.hot_window_ms, kv_min_quality_threshold.
risks: Quality regressions in long-tail prompts leading to customer-facing hallucinations if INT4 enabled without careful canarying.
Dequant CPU/GPU overhead may push latency over tight SLOs for low-latency tier customers — need per-variant p95 budgets.
Complexity in model onboarding: per-head calibration increases onboarding time and storage of extra metadata.
Edge-case corruption risk during network transfer of packed blobs — mitigated with checksums but adds operational complexity.
mitigations: Feature-flagged rollout and canarying on internal traffic + small subset of Dedicated customers.
Automatic fallback: if runtime detects increase in kv_quality_regressions_count > threshold, revert uses of compressed KV for that model/version.
Per-head calibration script included in onboarding pipeline; produce a head-sensitivity map artifact that is versioned with the model.
Add periodic checksum verification background job and an alert for any detection of mismatch.
next_steps: Merge runtime PR #2483 after addressing micro-benchmark comments (Leo).
Add head-sensitivity calibration to the model onboarding CI (Aisha + Priya).
Run a 48-hour canary against internal production traces with hybrid settings; collect kv_quality_regressions_count and p95 latency (Marcus to schedule).
Document config knobs and recommended defaults in Console docs and expose a cost/quality slider for Dedicated customers (PM: Elena Rivera).
Plan a follow-up ticket to explore learned quantization (per-chunk learned scale factors) if hybrid approach meets SLOs (ENG-7601).
